Subject: POC environment alignment & ops checklist — FictiCorp

Thanks for a productive discovery call today — appreciate the thorough context on your API volume and the latency targets.

Recap & recommended next steps

- Goal for the POC: validate latency <= 200ms p50 for your synchronous CRM enrichment calls, test end-to-end dataflow, and confirm identical outputs vs your baseline for 10k token window.
- Success criteria (high level):
  1) Latency: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 450ms under expected concurrency (10 concurrent workers).
  2) Cost proxy: token cost <= $0.003 per 1k tokens for inference layer (target).
  3) Quality: zero regression on our shared prompt set (sample folder in Drive).
  4) Integration: developer onboarding + test harness running within 2 weeks of env provisioning.

Environment options we discussed

- Hosted (fastest): Redwood hosted API — minimal setup, 48–72h to start, easiest for initial quality + latency checks. Good to iterate prompts quickly.
- Dedicated sandbox (recommended for this workload): Reserved GPU pool in Redwood Dedicated — predictable throughput for concurrency testing, supports KV caching and longer context. 3–5 business days to provision once contract/commit is agreed.
- VPC trial (preferred for security/compliance): Customer VPC/private control plane — best for data residency and stricter networking controls. Requires networking work on your side (peering / customer firewall rules). Estimate 7–12 business days for full setup.

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline

Week 0 (this week): finalize environment choice and sign attached POC checklist. 
Week 1: Provision environment + ingress tests (Dylan to own provisioning).
Week 2: Run baseline tests (latency, throughput), iterate prompts, and log outputs to shared Drive.
Week 3: Final regression check + handover to your engineering for validation.

Ownership

- Redwood PM: Soojin Lee (soojin.lee@redwood.com) — overall POC coordination and success criteria.
- Redwood Infra lead: Dylan Brooks (dylan.brooks@redwood.com) — environment provisioning and network coordination.
- Redwood Solutions Eng: Karthik Iyer (karthik.iyer@redwood.com) — trial configuration, quantization/slotting recommendations.

Requests for you

- Confirm preferred environment (Hosted / Dedicated sandbox / VPC trial) by EOD Thursday.
- Share a contact for your network/security lead to start pre-work for VPC if you choose that route.
- Tell us any must-have compliance docs (e.g., SOC 2 in-scope controls) we should attach — I included a SOC 2 summary below.

Attachments: POC-success-criteria.md, trial-environment-options.pdf

Thanks — I’ll schedule the short ops kickoff once you confirm the environment.

Emily — adding more color from an engineering/ops perspective.

Short summary: VPC trial is straightforward but has two tracks depending on whether you want full private data plane or just peered access to Redwood-managed endpoints.

1) Quick option (peered access):
   - Redwood exposes endpoints in a dedicated subnet and we set up VPC peering (or VPC Private Service Connect in GCP/Azure Private Link equivalent).
   - Client provides CIDR ranges and an SSH jump box is optional. Minimal firewall changes: outbound to Redwood's peering ranges on ports 443 and 8443.
   - Provision time: ~5–7 business days if your network team can respond quickly.

2) Full private control plane (air-gapped-like):
   - Requires customer network config + routing + optional on-prem package. Best for regulated workloads.
   - Provision time: 10–14 business days; we’ll need a network runbook and an SSO/KMS handshake window.

Dedicated sandbox vs Hosted cost (ballpark for a 3-week POC with moderate token usage):
- Hosted: $1.2k–$2.4k (depends on token volume, no reserved capacity)
- Dedicated sandbox: $3.8k–$6.0k (reserved GPU pool to keep p95 latency stable under concurrency)

Pre-work checklist (network & ops):
- Share network contact and preferred CIDR ranges.
- Provide a dev/test service account for integration tests (or allow OAuth redirect for our test harness).
- Confirm whether you need logs exported to your SIEM (we support Splunk/Datadog forwarding).

I attached: redwood-vpc-template.yaml (sample network template) and the SOC 2 summary for your security team.

I'll sync with Dylan on provisioning slots once you confirm.
